- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline in forecast, it often overcorrects; cap peak forecast at 1.5x recent high or adjust downward by 3–5% after spike.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is low (≤0.33) or shows negative sentiment drift; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- Forecast horizon 30d often exhibits lag: model tends to be 1–3 days behind true trend; adjust by adding 0.5–1.0% to forecast for each lagged day.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or 0.33 values, model tends to underestimate; apply upward bias of 1–2% to compensate for sentiment-induced underreaction.
- Avoid forecasting above 82.00 unless sentiment is >0.80 and recent price is >80.00; cap forecasts at 82.50 to prevent over-optimism in bullish sentiment.
